code.router.http.why: Get a response for each HTTP request sent to the service.
code.router.http.how: Matches the request path and method to a handler and returns its response.

code.router.path.why: Find the route whose path template matches the request URI and capture its parameters.
code.router.path.how: Keeps one table of path templates mapped to endpoints and resolves a request path to an endpoint id.

code.router.method.why: Pick the handler for the request's HTTP method once the path is matched.
code.router.method.how: Each path in the router holds one method router that dispatches by method and answers 405 with an Allow header when none matches.

code.endpoint.route.why: Dispatch the request to an endpoint that may be any tower service, not only a handler.
code.endpoint.route.how: Stores each endpoint as a boxed, cloneable service and clones it per request; nest, merge, fallback and layer all operate on these.

upstream.library.layer.why: Wrap all routes, or only matched routes, in middleware.
upstream.library.layer.how: Router::layer and route_layer accept any tower Layer and apply it to each stored endpoint.

upstream.library.service.why: Be usable as a standard service by any tower-compatible server or test harness.
upstream.library.service.how: Implements Service for requests so Router can be called, nested or composed with other services.

code.service.make.why: Hand the router to a server that builds one service per connection.
code.service.make.how: into_make_service and into_make_service_with_connect_info wrap the router in a make service that clones it per connection.

upstream.library.service.why: Call the wrapped endpoint through the standard service interface.
upstream.library.service.how: Wraps a BoxCloneSyncService so every endpoint has the same request, response and error types.

code.endpoint.route.why: Dispatch the request to an endpoint that may be any tower service, not only a handler.
code.endpoint.route.how: Stores each endpoint as a boxed, cloneable service and clones it per request; nest, merge, fallback and layer all operate on these.

upstream.library.layer.why: Wrap all routes, or only matched routes, in middleware.
upstream.library.layer.how: Router::layer and route_layer accept any tower Layer and apply it to each stored endpoint.

upstream.library.service.why: Be usable as a standard service by any tower-compatible server or test harness.
upstream.library.service.how: Implements Service for requests so Router can be called, nested or composed with other services.

code.service.make.why: Hand the router to a server that builds one service per connection.
code.service.make.how: into_make_service and into_make_service_with_connect_info wrap the router in a make service that clones it per connection.

upstream.library.service.why: Call the wrapped endpoint through the standard service interface.
upstream.library.service.how: Wraps a BoxCloneSyncService so every endpoint has the same request, response and error types.

code.handler.request.why: Run the handler registered for the matched HTTP method.
code.handler.request.how: get, post, put and the other method functions wrap a handler and store it in a slot for that method, with an optional fallback.

code.endpoint.route.why: Store each method's handler or service in a uniform callable form.
code.endpoint.route.how: Each method slot holds a Route; a handler is converted into one with the router state.

upstream.library.path_matcher.why: Resolve a request path against many path templates with captures and wildcards.
upstream.library.path_matcher.how: Inserts each template into a matchit tree and returns the route id and captured URL parameters for a path.

code.router.method.why: Hold the method router for each matched path.
code.router.method.how: Maps each route id to an endpoint, either a method router or a service, and calls it with the captured parameters stored in the request extensions.

code.endpoint.route.why: Dispatch to nested routers or services mounted under a prefix.
code.endpoint.route.how: nest strips the prefix with a strip-prefix service and mounts the inner router at a wildcard path.

code.extractor.request.why: Build each handler argument from the incoming request.
code.extractor.request.how: Handler is implemented for async functions of up to 16 arguments; each argument type is extracted in order and the last may consume the body.

code.converter.response.why: Turn the handler return value into an HTTP response.
code.converter.response.how: The future output is passed to into_response, so any type that implements IntoResponse can be returned.

code.extractor.path.why: Receive typed values for the path template captures.
code.extractor.path.how: Deserializes captured URL parameters into a tuple, struct or map; rejects with 400 or 500 when parsing fails.

code.extractor.query.why: Receive typed values from the URL query string.
code.extractor.query.how: Deserializes the query string into the target type; rejects with 400 on failure.

code.extractor.json.why: Receive a typed request body and send typed response bodies as JSON.
code.extractor.json.how: As extractor, requires a JSON content type, buffers the body and deserializes it; as IntoResponse, serializes the value with a JSON content type.

code.extractor.form.why: Receive typed values from form submissions.
code.extractor.form.how: Reads the query for GET and HEAD, otherwise the url-encoded body, and deserializes it; also serializes as a response.

code.extractor.state.how: Clones the state given to Router::with_state, or a part of it through FromRef.

code.extractor.extension.why: Share values that middleware attached to the request, and attach values to responses.
code.extractor.extension.how: Reads one typed value from the request extensions; as a layer it inserts a value into each request.

code.extractor.multipart.why: Receive file uploads and multi-field form bodies.
code.extractor.multipart.how: Streams the multipart/form-data body field by field.

code.extractor.connect_info.why: Learn the peer address or connection details of the client.
code.extractor.connect_info.how: Reads a value placed in request extensions by a make service built with into_make_service_with_connect_info.

code.extractor.matched_path.why: Learn which route template matched the request.
code.extractor.matched_path.how: Reads the path template the router stored in request extensions, for logging or metrics.

code.extractor.websocket.why: Upgrade an HTTP request to a WebSocket connection.
code.extractor.websocket.how: Validates the handshake headers, returns a 101 response and passes the upgraded connection to a callback.

code.extractor.original_uri.why: Read the request URI before any nest prefix was removed.
code.extractor.original_uri.how: Reads the URI stored in request extensions by the router before nesting rewrites it.

code.extractor.nested_path.why: Read the prefix under which the current router is nested.
code.extractor.nested_path.how: Reads the nested path stored in request extensions by nest.

code.extractor.raw_query.why: Read the query string without parsing.
code.extractor.raw_query.how: Returns the query string as an optional string.

code.extractor.raw_form.why: Read the form payload without parsing.
code.extractor.raw_form.how: Returns the form bytes from the query or body.

code.router.path.why: Get the URL parameters captured when the path was matched.
code.router.path.how: Reads the captured parameters the path router stored in the request extensions.

upstream.library.serialization.why: Convert captured strings to typed values.
upstream.library.serialization.how: Uses a serde deserializer over the captured key and value pairs.

upstream.library.serialization.why: Convert the query string to a typed value.
Convert between typed values and JSON.
upstream.library.serialization.how: Uses serde_json with serde_path_to_error so errors name the failing field.

code.body.http.why: Read the complete request body before deserializing.
code.body.http.how: Collects the body bytes, subject to the default body limit.

upstream.library.serialization.why: Convert url-encoded form data to a typed value.

code.body.http.why: Read the form body for non-GET requests.
code.body.http.how: Collects the body bytes, subject to the default body limit.
Wraps the body data stream in a multer parser.

upstream.library.multipart.how: Delegates field iteration and boundary handling to multer.

code.router.http.why: Receive the state the router was given.
code.router.http.how: Router::with_state captures the state and passes it to every handler and extractor as the S parameter.

code.service.make.why: Receive connection details from the server.
code.service.make.how: The make service inserts a ConnectInfo extension built from each accepted connection.

code.router.path.how: The path router stores the template in extensions after each match.

upstream.library.http.why: Take over the connection after the 101 response.
upstream.library.http.how: Uses hyper's upgrade future to obtain the raw connection.

upstream.library.websocket.how: Wraps the upgraded connection in a tungstenite stream and exposes it as WebSocket with Message values.

code.router.path.how: The path router stores it in extensions before it strips a nest prefix.
The path router stores it in extensions when it mounts a nested router.

code.body.http.how: Collects the body bytes for non-GET requests.

code.middleware.function.why: Let the application add cross-cutting request logic as plain async functions.
code.middleware.function.how: Router::layer accepts from_fn layers; the function receives the request and a Next value to call the rest of the stack.

upstream.library.layer.why: Be applied to routers, method routers and handlers as a layer.
upstream.library.layer.how: Implements tower Layer and Service around the inner service.

upstream.library.layer.why: Be applied to routers, method routers and handlers as a layer.
upstream.library.layer.how: Implements tower Layer and Service around the inner service.

upstream.library.layer.why: Be applied to routers, method routers and handlers as a layer.
upstream.library.layer.how: Implements tower Layer and Service around the inner service.

upstream.library.layer.why: Be applied to routers, method routers and handlers as a layer.
upstream.library.layer.how: Implements tower Layer and Service around the inner service.

code.extractor.request.why: Run extractors on the request before calling the next middleware.
code.extractor.request.how: Function arguments before Next are extracted like handler arguments.

code.extractor.request.why: Run extractors on the request before rewriting it.
code.extractor.request.how: Function arguments are extracted like handler arguments.

code.converter.response.why: Reject the request early with a response.
code.converter.response.how: The function may return a Result whose error is converted to a response.

code.converter.response.why: Convert the mapped result back into a response.
code.converter.response.how: The function return value is converted with into_response.

code.extractor.request.why: Run extractors alongside the response being mapped.
code.extractor.request.how: Function arguments before the response are extracted from the request parts.

code.extractor.request.why: Use an extractor only to accept or reject the request.
code.extractor.request.how: Runs the extractor and discards its value, returning the rejection response on failure.

code.handler.error.why: Turn the errors of fallible services into responses so the router stays infallible.
code.handler.error.how: Router::route_service and layer require infallible services; HandleError converts an error to a response through a handler function.

code.extractor.request.why: Pass the request parts to the error function.
code.extractor.request.how: The error function arguments are extracted like handler arguments before the error value.

code.converter.response.why: Produce the response for an error.
code.converter.response.how: The error function return value is converted with into_response.

upstream.library.layer.why: Wrap a fallible layer stack at the point where it is applied.

code.body.http.why: Place response data in a body.
code.body.http.how: Strings, bytes, JSON and streams are all converted to the axum Body type.

code.stream.event.how: Sse implements IntoResponse and sets the text/event-stream headers.

code.response.redirect.how: Redirect::to, temporary and permanent set the status code and Location header.

upstream.library.http.why: Keep the response body streaming over the connection.
upstream.library.http.how: The event stream is an HTTP body that hyper writes as chunks.

code.service.make.why: Create a service for each accepted connection.
code.service.make.how: Calls the make service with the incoming stream, then drives the resulting service per request.

code.listener.network.how: Loops on Listener::accept for TCP, Unix socket or custom listeners and retries after accept errors.

upstream.library.http.why: Parse HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 on each connection.
upstream.library.http.how: Runs hyper-util's auto connection builder on every accepted stream, with optional graceful shutdown.

upstream.runtime.async.how: Spawns one tokio task per connection and uses a watch channel to signal graceful shutdown.

upstream.runtime.async.why: Wait for new connections on a socket.
upstream.runtime.async.how: TcpListener and UnixListener implement Listener over tokio sockets.

upstream.library.service.why: Produce clones of the router as services.
upstream.library.service.how: Implements Service for any target and returns a clone of the inner service.

upstream.library.http.why: Carry request and response bytes in the type hyper uses.
upstream.library.http.how: Body wraps a boxed http-body so incoming hyper bodies and custom bodies share one type.

code.server.http.why: Reach the service over a network connection.
code.server.http.how: Connects over TCP and exchanges HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 messages.

code.router.http.why: Load pages, submit forms, follow redirects and keep long-lived streams open.
code.router.http.how: Sends form posts and requests for event streams and WebSocket upgrades, and follows Redirect responses.

code.extractor.query.why: Receive typed values or the raw string from the URL query.
code.extractor.query.how: Query deserializes the query string with serde and rejects with 400 on failure; RawQuery returns the unparsed string as an option.

code.extractor.form.why: Receive typed form values or raw form bytes.
code.extractor.form.how: Form reads the query for GET and HEAD, otherwise the url-encoded body, and deserializes it, and is also a response type; RawForm returns the unparsed bytes.

code.extractor.matched_path.why: Learn where the request matched in the routing tree.
code.extractor.matched_path.how: MatchedPath gives the route template; OriginalUri gives the URI before a nest prefix was removed; NestedPath gives the nest prefix. The router stores each in request extensions.

code.middleware.function.why: Let the application add cross-cutting request and response logic as plain async functions.
code.middleware.function.how: from_fn wraps a function that receives extracted arguments, the request and Next; map_request rewrites or rejects the request; map_response rewrites the response; from_extractor runs an extractor only to accept or reject.

code.converter.response.why: Produce an early response or a changed response.
code.converter.response.how: Function return values, including rejections from map_request and from_extractor, are converted with into_response.

upstream.library.macro.why: Derive extractor implementations and diagnose handler type errors.
upstream.library.macro.how: The derive macros FromRequest, FromRequestParts and FromRef and the debug_handler attribute are re-exported behind the macros feature.

code.router.path.why: Find the route for the request, merge or nest other routers, and fall back when nothing matches.
code.router.path.how: Keeps one table of path templates mapped to endpoints; route, nest, merge and fallback edit it; an unmatched path goes to the fallback, by default a 404, and a path with the wrong method gets 405.
